newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says it postponing debut Samurai issue.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it postponing debut Samurai issue.

text.p: Israel said on Tuesday it was postponing a debut samurai bond issue planned for next month, citing a Japanese investigation of suspected illegal deals by lead manager Nomura Securities.
"Accountant-General Shy Talmon announced the Samurai bond issue planned for early June is being postponed," the Israeli Treasury said in a statement.

"(Talmon) added the planned issue will take place this year but setting a new date for the launch will depend on developments in Japan on one hand and will take into account strategic planning of international funding activities of Israel on the other hand," the Treasury said.

It said the postponement stemmed "from the fact that the Japanese Finance Ministry has not yet announced its decision about measures it is taking against Nomura Securities, which is suspected of illegal transactions in violation of the Japanese Securities and Exchange law".
Israel announced in March it intended to raise 15 billion to 20 billion yen in the samurai market and selected Nomura to lead manage the transaction.
"Rumours of possible sanction, likely to affect the planned (Israeli) issue, include suspension of Nomura's activities in the capital market," the Treasury said.

"This would not allow Israel's bonds to be distributed among institutional investors in an optimal way, and in this case the objectives set when penetrating a market for the first time would not be achieved," the statement said.
Prosecutors and Japan's securities watchdog are investigating Nomura over suspected illegal deals linked to corporate racketeers.
